title: 🔁 Practice Plus: relative clauses & comparatives review

questions.prompt: Complete: "The man ___ lives next door is a doctor."
questions.explanation: "The man" is a person, so the relative pronoun is "who" (or "that"): the man who lives next door. "Which" refers only to things, and "what" and "when" are question words.

questions.prompt: Complete: "The river ___ runs near our village is polluted."
questions.explanation: "The river" is a thing, so the relative pronoun is "which" (or "that"): the river which runs near our village. "Which it" gives "runs" a second subject, "who" is only for people, and "what" cannot follow a noun as a relative pronoun.

questions.prompt: Complete: "The smoke is dangerous for children ___ live near the factory."
questions.explanation: "That" can refer to people, so it fits after "children": children that live near the factory ("who" would fit too). "Which" is only for things, "what" never follows a noun to define it, and "they" does not join the two parts.

questions.prompt: Complete: "This book is ___ than the last one I read." (interesting)
questions.explanation: "Interesting" is a long adjective, so its comparative is "more interesting" (than). "Interestinger" adds -er to a long adjective, "most" belongs to the superlative, and "more interestinger" uses both marks at once.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Of all the days of the week, Monday is ___ day for me." (hard)
questions.explanation: Monday is compared with every day of the week, so we need the superlative: "hard" is short, so the hardest. "The harder" is a comparative, "hardest" forgets "the", and "the most" is only for long adjectives.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My new phone is ___ my old one; they cost the same." (expensive)
questions.explanation: "They cost the same" means equality: as + plain adjective + as, as expensive as. "More expensive than" says one costs more, "than" never closes an equality, and "more" never goes inside as … as.
